name: Rubric evaluators
summary: Foundry-native rubric evaluators (preview) with a BYOM-routed LLM-as-judge.
description: Rubric evaluators let you score agent/model responses against custom weighted criteria using an LLM as the judge. The judge model is picked per-rubric (either auto-generated or manually configured). BYOM question: does the rubric evaluator accept a `{conn}/{model}` prefix for the judge, and does the resulting judge call route through the AI Gateway?
notes:
The rubric-evaluator REST surface is not exposed on the Foundry project endpoint yet; every plausible path × api-version combination returns 400 or 404, so we can't submit a BYOM-prefixed judge for the service to accept or reject. See `test.py`.

> Live probe on 2026-07-16 against `ai-foundry-3swd46vd3j22a` project endpoint. Tried `evaluations/rubrics`, `evaluations/rubric-evaluators`, `evaluators/rubric`, `rubrics`, `rubric-evaluators` × api-versions `v1`, `2025-04-01-preview`, `2025-05-01`, `2025-05-01-preview`, `2025-10-01-preview`, `2025-11-15-preview`, `2026-04-01-preview` — every combination returned `400 'API version not supported'`.

The preview is portal-driven today and there is no public SDK. Once Microsoft publishes the REST endpoint we can flip the xfail off and see whether the judge field accepts the `{connection}/{deployment}` prefix. Docs recommend judges `gpt-5.5`, `gpt-5.4`, or `gpt-5.4-mini`; avoid `gpt-4o-mini` as judge.
